# Relative root groups generated by absolute root groups: proof

Worker 3483 (author of the proof, shared draft revision 10 of Task 3483); submitted
by Worker 4896 for Task 5518.

`Langlands.GroupScheme.relativeRootGroupAbsoluteGeneration.{u}` proves the
published proposition
`Langlands.GroupScheme.RelativeRootGroupAbsoluteGenerationStatement.{u}`
(module `Langlands.GroupScheme.Rational.RelativeRootGroupAbsoluteGenerationStatement`).
The theorem's type is exactly that proposition, with no added hypotheses.

## The statement

Let `k ⊆ K` be fields, write `b = algebraBaseMap k K`, and let `G` be a
connected reductive group over `k`, `i : S ⟶ G` a maximal split torus and
`j : T ⟶ G` a maximal torus with `f : S ⟶ T` and `groupHom f ≫ j = i`.
Suppose `T` splits over `K`. For a relative root `a`, call a root `β` of
`(G_K, T_K)` *above `a`* when `f_K ≫ β = n • a_K` for some natural number
`n > 0`. The statement asserts:

1. `RelativeRoot.subgroup j_K β ≤ (RelativeRoot.subgroup i a).baseChange b`
   for every root `β` above `a`;
2. every closed subgroup `h : H ⟶ G_K` whose range contains
   `RelativeRoot.subgroup j_K β` for every root `β` above `a` also contains
   `(RelativeRoot.subgroup i a).baseChange b`.

This is Borel–Tits, *Groupes réductifs* (1965), 3.8 (ii), 3.13 b) and 5.2
(source ID `borel-tits-1965-groupes-reductifs`); the statement's own Markdown
gives the quotations and the comparison with Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017),
25.19.

## The proof

The proof follows the route of Borel–Tits: the subgroup generated by the
absolute root groups above `a` is a smooth connected closed subgroup of
`U_(a)` with the same Lie algebra, so it equals `U_(a)`. Every step is carried
out with published Library results; the module adds seven auxiliary lemmas
in the namespace `Langlands.GroupScheme.RelativeRoot`, three of them private.

### Auxiliary lemmas over an arbitrary base

Let `B` be a scheme, `S` and `T` commutative group schemes over `B`, `G` a
group scheme over `B`, `f : S ⟶ T` and `j : T.toGrp ⟶ G`.

- `orbit_comp_torusHom`. For a point `g : U ⟶ G`, precomposing the
  conjugation orbit map `orbit j g : U × T ⟶ G` with `U ◁ f` gives
  `orbit (groupHom f ≫ j) g`. The proof unfolds `orbit`, rewrites the
  conjugation action with the published `AutomorphicAction.conjugation_act`
  (`(conjugation i).act h g = (h ≫ i) * g * (h ≫ i)⁻¹`), and simplifies with
  Mathlib's `MonObj.comp_mul`, `GrpObj.comp_inv` and the whiskering lemmas.
- `subgroup_le_subgroup_comp_torusHom`. For every character `β` of `T`,
  `subgroup j β ≤ subgroup (groupHom f ≫ j) (f ≫ β)` on every test scheme.
  An orbit extension `e : U × 𝔸¹ ⟶ G` of `g` through `β` is also an orbit
  extension through `f ≫ β` for the restricted action: precompose its defining
  equation with `U ◁ f` and use `orbit_comp_torusHom`. The value of `e` at
  `0` is unchanged.
- `subgroup_le_subgroup_comp_torusHom_of_nsmul`. If `f ≫ β = n • a` with
  `n > 0`, then `subgroup j β ≤ subgroup (groupHom f ≫ j) a`. This combines
  the previous lemma with the published `RelativeRoot.subgroup_nsmul_le`
  (`subgroup i (n • a) ≤ subgroup i a` for `n > 0`).
- Private `factorsThrough_of_range_le` and `range_le_of_factorsThrough`. For
  homomorphisms `a : A ⟶ G` and `q : H ⟶ G`,
  `SubgroupFunctor.range a ≤ SubgroupFunctor.range q` holds if and only if
  the underlying morphism of `a` factors through `q`. The first direction
  applies the inclusion to the identity point of `A` and uses
  `factorsThrough_iff_containsImage` and `SubgroupFunctor.containsImage_iff`;
  the second composes the factorization with each point.

### Auxiliary lemmas over a field

Now let `F` be a field, `S` and `T` commutative group schemes over `Spec F`
and `G` a smooth affine group scheme over `Spec F`.

- Private `nsmul_ne_zero_of_isSplitTorus`. If `S` is split, `a ≠ 0` and
  `n > 0`, then `n • a ≠ 0`. A splitting gives integer coordinates
  `splitTorusCharacterCoordinates e : characterLattice S ≃+ (I → ℤ)`, and
  `ℤ` has no zero divisors.
- `subgroup_comp_torusHom_le_range_of_roots`. Assume `S` and `T` split,
  `a ≠ 0`, and let `h : H ⟶ G` be a closed subgroup whose range contains
  `subgroup j β` for every `β ∈ roots j` with `f ≫ β = n • a` for some
  `n > 0`. Then `subgroup (groupHom f ≫ j) a ≤ SubgroupFunctor.range h`.

The proof of the last lemma has six steps. Let `J` be the type of roots `β` of
`j` with `f ≫ β = n • a` for some `n > 0`, and write `U_a` for
`subgroup (groupHom f ≫ j) a`.

1. *Representatives.* For each `β ∈ J`, `β ≠ 0` because it is a root, so the
   published `RelativeRoot.subgroup_isSmoothConnectedClosed_of_ne_zero`
   (applied to the split torus `T`) gives a smooth connected group `C β` and a
   closed subgroup `incl β : C β ⟶ G` representing `subgroup j β`. Each
   `C β` is affine over `Spec F`, because `incl β` is a closed immersion into
   the affine `G`. The same lemma for the split torus `S` and `a ≠ 0` gives a
   closed representative of `U_a`.
2. *The generated subgroup.* The published
   `FiniteGeneration.exists_smooth_generated_family` gives a smooth connected
   group `D` and `d : D ⟶ G` with `IsGeneratedByFamily C incl d`: `d` is a
   closed subgroup, every `incl β` factors through `d`, and
   `SubgroupFunctor.range d ≤ SubgroupFunctor.range q` for every closed
   subgroup `q` through which all `incl β` factor.
3. *`range d ≤ U_a`.* Each `subgroup j β` with `β ∈ J` lies in `U_a` by
   `subgroup_le_subgroup_comp_torusHom_of_nsmul`, so each `incl β` factors
   through the closed representative of `U_a`, and minimality gives the
   inclusion. Conversely `subgroup j β ≤ range d` for every `β ∈ J`, because
   `incl β` factors through `d`.
4. *Lie algebra of `U_a`.* By the published
   `RelativeRoot.tangentSubmodule_subgroup`, the tangent submodule of `U_a`
   is the span of the weight spaces of the restricted action for the
   characters `n • a`, `n ≥ 1` (`semigroupWeightSpan` over `cyclicTail a 1`).
   By the published `semigroupWeightSpan_comp_torusHom`, this equals the span
   of the weight spaces `weightSpace j χ` over the characters `χ` of `T` with
   `f ≫ χ ∈ cyclicTail a 1` (`characterSemigroupPreimage`).
5. *Lie algebra of `range d`.* Its tangent submodule is contained in that of
   `U_a` by step 3 and `tangentSubmodule_mono`. For the reverse inclusion, let
   `χ` be a character of `T` with `f ≫ χ = n • a`, `n > 0`. Its action weight
   space is `weightSpace j χ` (`actionWeightSpace_conjugation`). If this is
   `⊥` there is nothing to show. Otherwise `χ ≠ 0`, since `f ≫ 0 = 0` while
   `n • a ≠ 0`; so `χ` is a root in `J`. Then `weightSpace j χ` lies in the
   span over `cyclicTail χ 1`, which is the tangent submodule of
   `subgroup j χ` (`tangentSubmodule_subgroup` for the split torus `T`),
   which lies in the tangent submodule of `range d` by step 3.
6. *Conclusion.* `range d` is smooth connected closed, represented by `d`
   (a closed immersion is a monomorphism), and so is `U_a` by step 1. The two
   have the same tangent submodule (`hasLieImage_iff_tangentSubmodule_eq`
   turns this into `HasLieImage`), and `range d ≤ U_a`, so the published
   `IsSmoothConnectedClosed.eq_of_le_of_hasLieImage` gives `range d = U_a`.
   Every `incl β` factors through `h` by the hypothesis on `h`, so
   minimality of `d` gives `U_a = range d ≤ range h`.

### The main theorem

The proof introduces the hypotheses and makes `IsAffineHom` and `Smooth`
instances for `G` from the fields `IsConnectedReductive.isAffineHom` and
`IsConnectedReductive.smooth`. For `G_K`, it makes the `Smooth` instance
explicitly: its structure morphism is a pullback of that of `G`, and Mathlib
gives smoothness of the pullback. The `IsAffineHom` instance for `G_K`, needed
when `subgroup_comp_torusHom_le_range_of_roots` is applied over `K`, is found
by instance search: it is the published instance
`IdentityComponent.isAffineHom_baseChange`. The proof then fixes
`a ∈ relativeRoots i` and records:

- `S` is split (`hi.1.1`), so `S_K` is split (`IsSplitTorus.baseChange`);
- `a_K ≠ 0`, because `characterLattice.baseChangeEquiv b S` is an additive
  equivalence for split `S` and `a ≠ 0` (first component of
  `a ∈ relativeRoots i`);
- `i_K = groupHom f_K ≫ j_K`, by `hf` and functoriality of base change;
- `(RelativeRoot.subgroup i a).baseChange b` equals
  `RelativeRoot.subgroup (groupHom f_K ≫ j_K) a_K`, by the previous point and
  the published `RelativeRoot.subgroup_baseChange`.

After rewriting with the last equality, conjunct 1 is
`subgroup_le_subgroup_comp_torusHom_of_nsmul` over `Spec K`, and conjunct 2 is
`subgroup_comp_torusHom_le_range_of_roots` over `K` with the split tori
`S_K` and `T_K`.

Only part of the hypotheses is used: `G` enters only through being smooth and
affine, `i` only through `S` being split, and `a` only through `a ≠ 0`. The
maximality of `j` (`IsMaximalTorus j`) is not used and is left unnamed.

The option `backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false` is set for
`subgroup_comp_torusHom_le_range_of_roots` and for the main theorem only.
The theorem depends only on the axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice` and
`Quot.sound`.
